items.title: An abelian category has all finite limits and colimits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file homology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every abelian category has all finite limits and all finite colimits (statement lines 901-905). The proof is a complete argument: the existence of finite limits is reduced, through a named criterion, to finite products, which exist by definition, and to equalizers, which are identified with the kernel of the difference of the two morphisms and hence exist (proof lines 907-913); the statement for finite colimits is dual (proof line 914). The non-formal content is the identification of equalizers with kernels. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
